claim: The llm-d Router EPP reads the exact header name `x-llm-d-inference-objective` to identify the InferenceObjective resource whose priority and performance goals apply to the request.
stance_target: exact header name for priority/objective routing in llm-d Router
scope_conditions: llm-d Router v0.9 (latest) EPP HTTP header API reference
quoted_support: `x-llm-d-inference-objective` Specifies the name of the `InferenceObjective` resource associated with the request. The EPP uses this to look up the corresponding objective resource in the same namespace as the InferencePool to apply the defined priority and performance goals.

claim: The llm-d Router EPP reads the exact header name `x-llm-d-inference-fairness-id` to group requests for fairness-based flow control, defaulting to `default-flow` when the header is omitted.
stance_target: exact header name for fairness/tenant ID routing in llm-d Router
scope_conditions: llm-d Router v0.9 EPP HTTP header API reference
quoted_support: `x-llm-d-inference-fairness-id` Provides a unique identifier for grouping requests for fairness-based flow control. Requests with the same ID share capacity according to the fairness policy. If omitted, the EPP defaults to `default-flow`.

claim: The llm-d Router EPP reads the exact header name `x-llm-d-model-name-rewrite` as a per-request, client-supplied alternative to the server-side rule-based InferenceModelRewrite API for overriding the target model name.
stance_target: exact header name for model-name routing/rewrite in llm-d Router
scope_conditions: llm-d Router v0.9 EPP HTTP header API reference
quoted_support: `x-llm-d-model-name-rewrite` Specifies the target model name to be used for the request. This is an alternative approach to model name rewriting; while the `InferenceModelRewrite` API provides rule-based rewriting on the server side, this header allows for an explicit, per-request override.

claim: llm-d Router v0.9.0+ accepts deprecated header aliases x-gateway-inference-objective, x-gateway-inference-fairness-id, and x-gateway-model-name-rewrite as read-only compatibility names for the canonical x-llm-d-* headers, with the canonical header value winning if both are sent.
stance_target: llm-d-router header names differ from but map onto Azure-style x-gateway-* header conventions
scope_conditions: llm-d Router v0.9.0 and later; no announced removal date for aliases
quoted_support: llm-d Router v0.9.0 and later accept the previous EPP-managed header names as deprecated read aliases... If a request sends both a canonical header and its deprecated alias, the canonical `x-llm-d-*` value wins deterministically.

claim: The x-gateway-destination-endpoint* header family belongs to the separate Gateway API Inference Extension (GAIE) Endpoint Picker Protocol spec and is explicitly unchanged by the llm-d header rename.
scope_conditions: llm-d Router v0.9 EPP HTTP header API reference
quoted_support: This rename applies only to llm-d/EPP-managed user and control headers. Gateway API Inference Extension (GAIE) Endpoint Picker Protocol headers, such as `x-gateway-destination-endpoint*`, are unchanged.

claim: The doc frames all EPP-inspected header values generically as standard incoming HTTP request headers rather than as values that must be derived exclusively from a Kubernetes CRD reconciler, implying an upstream proxy or gateway plugin could set them directly.
stance_target: these headers can be set by an upstream proxy/gateway plugin instead of only being derived from a Kubernetes CRD
scope_conditions: llm-d Router v0.9 EPP HTTP header API reference, Implementation Notes section
quoted_support: Case Sensitivity: All header lookups are case-insensitive. Source: These values are typically provided as standard HTTP headers in the incoming request.

claim: The EPP sets a response header x-llm-d-request-dropped-reason only on 429 responses it generates itself (not forwarded from a model server), using a two-prefix scheme distinguishing pre-dispatch rejection (rejected-*) from post-dispatch eviction (evicted-*).
scope_conditions: llm-d Router v0.9 EPP HTTP header API reference
quoted_support: Indicates why a request was dropped by flow control. Only present on `429` responses generated by the EPP (not forwarded from a model server). The value uses a two-prefix scheme: `rejected-*` means the request never reached an inference server, `evicted-*` means it was dispatched and then killed.
